comments.content: `batch.Positions.Ints()` allocates a new slice on every call. Since this is called on every forward pass with multimodal input, consider caching the result or using a cheaper accessor. More importantly, if `batch.Positions` is nil (e.g., a batch without positions), this will panic. Verify that Positions is always populated before this path.
`batch.Positions.Ints()` is called inside the inner unwind loop, causing a fresh allocation on every iteration of `j`. Hoist it outside the `for j` loop to avoid repeated allocations.

`Ints()` uses `unsafe.Slice((*int32)(bts), ...)` for CPU-memory tensors, which returns a view into the underlying ggml buffer rather than a copy. Callers (e.g., `kvcache/causal.go` storing `c.curPositions`) may hold this slice beyond the tensor's lifetime, leading to use-after-free or aliasing bugs. Consider returning a copy, or document clearly that the returned slice is only valid while the tensor is alive. Note `Floats()` has the same pattern but is pre-existing.

The previous code guarded with `len(batch.Outputs) > 0` before assigning outputs. The new code unconditionally assigns `batch.Outputs` on the last block. If `batch.Outputs` is nil/empty (e.g., during a reserve/warmup pass where outputs aren't needed), downstream `Rows`/indexing may fail. Confirm that `batch.Outputs` is always a valid tensor here, or restore the length check.

`FromIntSlice(batchOutputs, len(batchOutputs))` is called even when `batchOutputs` is empty (no sequence at its last input). Verify that `FromIntSlice` with length 0 produces a valid tensor that downstream `Rows`/`FromIntSlice` consumers handle correctly; otherwise guard with a length check.

`ctx.Input().Arange(0, float32(s.parallel), 1, ml.DTypeI32)` — verify that `Arange` with `DTypeI32` produces the same values as the previous `[]int32{0,1,...,parallel-1}`. If `Arange` uses float32 internally, large `s.parallel` values could lose precision, though this is unlikely in practice.
